Option A, (∃x){(Kx • Px) • (∃y)[(Ey • Sy) • Hxy]}, is logically equivalent to this form. It states 'There exists an x such that x is a kind person, AND there exists a y such that y is an endangered species, AND x helps y.' Options B and C incorrectly assign predicates (e.g., Sx to people, Py to species) and C also reverses the helping relationship. Which of the given formulas of PL is the best symbolization of the following sentence?
Doctors are helpful unless their patients are rude.
model_reasoning: Let H be the proposition 'Doctors are helpful' and R be the proposition 'Their patients are rude'. The phrase 'A unless B' is logically equivalent to '~B -> A' or 'A v B'. In this case, 'Doctors are helpful unless their patients are rude' translates to '~R -> H' (If their patients are not rude, then doctors are helpful). The implication '~R -> H' is logically equivalent to 'R v H' (Their patients are rude or doctors are helpful). Therefore, H v R is the correct symbolization.
